body: The Grandview Heights Neighborhood Association and the West Palm Beach Neighborhood Alliance filed a complaint on October 14, 2026 in the 15th Judicial Circuit, alleging that Palm Beach County violated Florida's Government in the Sunshine Law when it approved financing for a planned convention center hotel, WPTV reported. The suit names Palm Beach County, several Related Ross affiliates, The Related Companies, L.P., the CityPlace Community Development District, the City of West Palm Beach and its Community Redevelopment Agency.

On September 29, 2026, the County Commission approved the 34-part deal 6-1. Commissioner Gregg Weiss, who represents the district where the hotel will stand, cast the only no vote. Under the deal, the county will advance $26 million from its General Fund reserves to a Related Ross affiliate as construction deposits, acquire the completed 18-story, 400-room hotel at 940 South Rosemary Avenue, and lease it back to Related for an initial 33-year term, with renewal options reaching as long as 97 years.

The plaintiffs say the item was placed on an "add-on" agenda six days before the vote, a procedure they argue is reserved for emergencies, and that the full 715-page transaction file was released at 8 a.m. on September 29, 90 minutes before the meeting began. According to the complaint, the county administrator acknowledged the county had "verbally agreed" with Related to hold the vote in September. The complaint also cites county consultant figures putting the present value of projected payments to the county over 97 years at about $275 million, roughly 3 percent of the nearly $8.5 billion figure officials cited. The groups ask the court to declare the approval void and to enjoin the county from executing, recording or funding the deal until the commission considers it at a properly noticed meeting with documents released in advance.

The county attorney told commissioners that the law requires a minimum of 24 hours' notice and that five days' notice was consistent with the county's agenda processes. Related Ross said in a statement that it believes the hotel is an example of "bringing new opportunities to the city for residents with local jobs." Residents had opposed the hotel earlier, including at a June 16, 2026 city planning board hearing, WPTV reported.

timeline.label: Residents oppose the hotel at a West Palm Beach Planning Board hearing
Palm Beach County Commission approves the 34-part hotel deal 6-1
Two neighborhood groups sue to void the approval under Florida's Sunshine Law
